title: Quantum Confined Luminescence in Two Dimensions
content: Nanoscale light emitters have emerged as a cornerstone of nanophotonics, promising revolutionary advances in lasers, light-emitting devices, and photodetectors. Conventional approaches to achieving localized emission have relied on quantum dots, nanowires, quantum wells, and point defects embedded within semiconductors or wide-bandgap materials. The spatial confinement inherent in these structures gives rise to quantized energy levels and unique emission properties, including single-photon emission in certain cases. These characteristics hold immense potential for applications in quantum communication, quantum cryptography, and advanced quantum light sources.
